newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut to hold new tender for 50,000 tonnes wheat.
newsitem.headline: Beirut to hold new tender for 50,000 tonnes wheat.

text.p: Lebanon's economy ministry said on Thursday it would hold a new tender for the purchase on its behalf of 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat on international markets next week.
"We will hold a new tender next Thursday for 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat," an offical of the Office of Cereals and Sugar Beet told Reuters.
He said bids would be for two shipments CIF to Beirut port silos of 25,000 tonnes each, the first between April 15 and May 10 and the second between June 20 and July 15.
The ministry last month rejected seven bids for the purchase of 35,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat, saying the prices from $203 to $207 per tonne were unsuitable.

The cereals office is part of the economy ministry, which periodically invites international grain companies or their Beirut agents to tender to buy wheat on the international markets on behalf of the Lebanese government.
Local firms also make purchases for the private sector.
Lebanon has yearly wheat requirements of 400,000 tonnes.
